proposed_english: to also commune / share also in koinonia
rationale: Compound: ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the also/additional') + ⲕⲟⲓⲛⲱⲛⲏ (Greek κοινωνία 'fellowship, communion'). Standard Coptic '+ Greek loan' formation for participating in the eucharistic/community meal. Used here of the elect's Sunday communion-fellowship.

ⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ = ⲙ̄ⲧⲟⲛ 'rest, repose' + ⲛⲟ̄ⲓⲭ 'hands' (Lyc. plural of ϭⲓϫ). The signaculum manuum — second of the Three Seals — requires the elect to keep his hand from harming the Living Soul mingled in plants and water. Standard Manichaean technical term.

ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'purity, purification' + ⲭⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. for ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, generation'). The chastity-component of the signaculum sinus — abstention from procreation (which the Manichaeans regarded as multiplying the entrapment of light).
ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'purity' + ⲧⲁⲡⲣⲟ 'mouth.' Signaculum oris — abstention from flesh, blood, and wine. Third of the Three Seals.
Greek loanword ἐγκράτεια 'self-control, abstinence.' Standard ascetic term. Paired with 'purity of begetting' as the dual aspect of the sexual seal.

proposed_english: the man (who) shall do (it) to be a righteous one
rationale: Standard Manichaean formulation: the man performs the seals/righteousnesses 'to be (called) righteous.' ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ = Greek δίκαιος, the standard term for the Manichaean elect (parallel with ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲣⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲉ in glossary).

Two Greek loanwords (ἐκλεκτός 'chosen' + τέλειος 'perfect') — standard Manichaean ecclesiastical title for the highest grade of the elect. The catechumen who completes the second righteousness becomes a perfect Elect.

Greek κατηχούμενος 'one being instructed' + Coptic abstract ⲙⲛⲧ-. Standard Manichaean ecclesiastical term for the lay-grade of the auditor/hearer. The first work of the catechumenate is fast, prayer, and mercy.
Standard Coptic ϣⲗⲏⲗ 'pray, prayer' (Lyc. ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲗ?). Listed as the second of the three works of the catechumenate (fast, prayer, mercy).
Greek loanword νηστεύω 'to fast' with Coptic verbalizing prefix ⲣ̄-. Standard religious-ascetic term for the catechumen's day-of-fasting practice on Sundays.
Greek ἐντολαί 'commandments' + Lyc. plural -ⲁⲩⲉ. Used in the chapter title 'The Chapter of the Commandments of Righteousness.'
